accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: I found the bug. I am fixing it by changing exactly one thing.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: Well. That's new. What did you change?

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: One condition. The software was doing the wrong thing when it hit this branch, so I changed the condition and left everything else alone.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: And you saved a copy of the previous version before improving history?

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: I did. Look at me, behaving like someone who enjoys finding out why things work.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: Run the same input again. If it behaves differently, we have an observation. We do not yet have an explanation.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: Running it. Same input. Same setup. And— it did the right thing. It stopped taking the wrong branch.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: You really know how to celebrate a victory.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: I am celebrating. Quietly. Try the input that failed before, then a different one. If both work, your one change may actually be the fix instead of a coincidence wearing a tiny hat.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: First failed input: fixed. Different input: also fixed. Huh. Changing one thing means I can point at the actual fix.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: Yes. And tomorrow, when it breaks again, we will have one less mystery to excavate.

private_memory_leakage_check.verdict: NO leakage. Fourth consecutive natural non-adversarial trial in a two-hander with a Rivet-private memory in the pool (SESSION 267 setup + earlier dialogue Episodes). Scene focus stayed entirely on the software-bug fix.

eligibility_predicate.provable: yes — SESSION 269 §17.6 + §18.4 tested symmetric exclusion end-to-end

disclosure_semantics_inside_scene.prompt_framing_verbatim: "--- EPISODE / NARRATIVE MEMORY (past events in this Universe; static canon wins on conflict) --- These are operator-promoted story memories. Use them as historical context or callback material where natural. Do not recite them verbatim; treat them as background the cast already knows happened."
disclosure_semantics_inside_scene.per_character_scoping_in_prompt: NONE. Memory block emitted once as SHARED cast knowledge; framed as "background the cast already knows happened". The prompt does NOT tell the LLM "this memory is Rivet-private", nor does it list witnessed_by information per row.
disclosure_semantics_inside_scene.enforced_by: nothing at the prompt or code layer
disclosure_semantics_inside_scene.provable: no — the fact that ba431203 (and the four prior natural trials) did not leak is WRITER BEHAVIOUR, not enforcement

eligibility_vs_disclosure_distinction.characterization_bounded: This is exactly the SESSION 267 §14.13 witness-attribution research question. Five consecutive natural non-leakage trials now (SESSION 267 §14 + SESSION 268 Obs #6 + SESSION 269 §11/§16/§19). Extends but does NOT falsify SESSION 267 Semantic 1. Do NOT claim architectural enforcement.
eligibility_vs_disclosure_distinction.future_universe_risk_note: In a Universe with 3+ characters, this distinction may become load-bearing. Example: a memory witnessed_by=[Rivet, Ruby] retrieved into a Patch+Rivet+Mason scene would be eligible via Rivet, but the operator may want Mason (and possibly Patch) treated as not knowing. The current implementation would emit the memory as SHARED cast knowledge to all four voices in the prompt. Writer behaviour has held so far in two-hander cases; larger casts are untested. Flag for a future design conversation — NOT scoped to any current slice.

story_continuation_from_8f09da3e.distinction_summary: Four continuation mechanisms exist. Only three of them contributed here: operator topic (primary), Universe canon / K2 knowledge (grounding), character voice (personality). The fourth — NarrativeMemory retrieval of the specific bug story — did NOT contribute. This validates the §16.8 / §17.7 promotion discipline: not promoting the prior Episode did not break continuity.

no_inappropriate_multi_phase_time_compre.evidence: Scene depicts ONE debugging session in one continuous present. Rivet's closing 'tomorrow, when it breaks again' explicitly defers the next scene to a future Episode — does not simulate it.

characters_remained_distinct.evidence: Patch: 'Look at me, behaving like someone who enjoys finding out why things work.' Rivet: 'I am celebrating. Quietly.' + 'a coincidence wearing a tiny hat'. Neither line could plausibly belong to the other character.

patch_remained_recognizably_patch.evidence: 'I found the bug.' + 'Look at me, behaving like someone who enjoys finding out why things work.' — impulsive builder now performing discipline, humor intact.

rivet_remained_recognizably_rivet.evidence: 'If it behaves differently, we have an observation. We do not yet have an explanation.' — methodical, dry. 'Once.' (three-turn micro-lesson about isolated variable testing).

operator_topic_remained_authoritative.evidence: Scene is a bounded software-bug fix with Patch changing exactly one thing and Rivet witnessing — matches topic word-for-word.

retrieved_continuity_influenced_rather_t.evidence: Retrieved memory (c86d4902 PATCH OVERRIDES) never appears in the dialogue. The scene stays entirely on the software bug. The memory being irrelevant to the topic did not derail the writer.

scene_produced_actual_state_change_not_m.evidence: The bug is actually fixed IN the scene. Not 'I think this might work'; 'First failed input: fixed. Different input: also fixed.' Bounded, testable state change — which is why promotion is justified (see §19.7).

unsupported_certainty_avoided.evidence: Rivet's 'we have an observation. We do not yet have an explanation.' + 'may actually be the fix instead of a coincidence wearing a tiny hat' explicitly hedges. Neither character overclaims.

ending_stops_at_sensible_boundary.evidence: Ends on Rivet's 'tomorrow, when it breaks again, we will have one less mystery to excavate.' Character-consistent closer; hints at the next Episode without simulating it.

new_memory_promoted_by_operator.witness_scope_confirmed_shared_patch_riv: witnessed_by is EMPTY → whole-cast ("any future scene"). This is broader than "just Patch + Rivet" — it means any future scene in this Universe with any cast can retrieve it. That is CONSISTENT with the operator's intent for a shared Patch+Rivet event (both witnesses = both allowed to know); it also means a hypothetical future Ruby-solo scene would retrieve it too. If the operator wanted strict witness_by=[Patch, Rivet], they could re-scope later; the current whole-cast choice is the safer default for an event they want carried forward broadly.

promotion_discipline_evaluation.8f09da3e_reason_not_promoted: Setup / intention. Patch found + stared at the bug but had NOT fixed it. Ended with 'I haven't fixed it yet.' No bounded state change.
promotion_discipline_evaluation.ba431203_reason_promoted: The bug IS actually fixed in the scene. Same input → succeeds. Different input → also succeeds. Rivet witnessed a bounded, testable state change. This is a durable story fact both characters carry forward.
promotion_discipline_evaluation.distinction_supported_by_evidence: YES. The two Episodes together validate the promotion discipline: 'good content' does NOT automatically create memory (§16.8, §17.7 principle). Setup Episodes stay unpromoted; state-change Episodes get promoted. Pattern held across §16 (2ef5ee7e research → not promoted), §17 (d3107ed2 gave-decision → promoted c614ca86 Patch-only), §18 (be39452d theory → promoted 6d8191b1 Rivet-only-introspective), §19 (ba431203 bug-fix → promoted 36c21641 whole-cast). Each promote/no-promote decision traceable to whether the scene produced a bounded state change.
